0.2.6.title: Masters keep their tags and their cover
0.2.6.summary: The artist, title and artwork now ride through the mastering chain, and a batch can say when it has finished.
highlights: Masters carry the source's tags and its cover art. A folder of covers named after the tracks can be used instead.
A new Tags & Artwork section in Personalize controls both.
A batch can be waited on rather than polled, and reports where every master landed.
Finished masters can be handed to Keystone, which imports them or points an existing track at them.

0.2.5.title: Output files keep their names
0.2.5.summary: A dot in a track title no longer cuts the output filename short, and two files can never land on the same one.
highlights: A title with a dot in it keeps its whole name: “Dom Dolla - Strangers ft. Mansionair” was being written as “Dom Dolla - Strangers ft.aiff”.
Two files that would be written to the same name are now kept apart, and you can choose what happens when a file is already there — replace it, skip it, or keep both.
A finished master reports its true peak and the ceiling it was made against, not just its loudness.

0.2.4.title: A window that reads as a surface, and an interface you can size
0.2.4.summary: The dark theme sits on the same ladder as Keystone and Stack, and the whole interface can be scaled to the display you are on.
highlights: Interface scale: Cmd / Ctrl with + and − size the whole window, not just the text. Cmd / Ctrl 0 goes back to 100%, and the size is remembered per display.
The dark theme's surfaces were lifted so the window reads as a surface rather than a hole, and now match Keystone and Stack rung for rung.
The status bar prints the build number beside the version, so two local builds of one version are no longer identical on screen.

0.2.3.title: An AI assistant can drive it, and a bad edit no longer resets a template
0.2.3.summary: Capstone's templates, settings and queue can be driven by an AI assistant, and an edit it cannot apply is now refused instead of quietly reverting your other settings.
highlights: Capstone can be read and driven by an AI assistant that speaks MCP: templates, output settings, the queue and starting a run.

An edit that cannot be applied is refused and your template is left alone. Before, one bad field could reset the target loudness, warmth, pitch correction and headroom to the Festival defaults and still report success.
Out-of-range values are clamped consistently now, including the limiter character.

0.2.0.title: Cover art, right-click and shareable templates
0.2.0.summary: The queue now looks like your library, every row has a menu, and a template is a file you can send to someone.
highlights: Album art shows next to every file in the queue.
Right-click a row to play it, reveal it, copy its path, re-analyze it or drop it.
Export a template to a file and import one back. No account, no sign-in.
A short tour on first launch, reopenable from the title bar.
Dark and light themes rebuilt for readability: no more unreadable greys or dimmed-out fields.
Version and a support link now sit along the bottom of the window.

0.1.0.title: First release
0.1.0.summary: Drop in a folder of finished tracks and get them back at one consistent volume, with clipped peaks repaired and the tags still on them.
highlights: Everything you process lands on the same loudness target, with a true-peak limiter so nothing distorts on the way there.
Clipped peaks are repaired before anything else touches the file.
Tracks sitting off concert pitch can be corrected, keeping the tempo or moving it with the pitch.
Optional warmth and multiband dynamics, saved into named templates you reuse.
Reads the formats a library is actually made of, writes AIFF, WAV, FLAC, ALAC or MP3, and carries your tags across.
Your originals are never touched: processed files are written somewhere new.
